findings.reason: Untrusted source: inject_data_ue_store (drivers/edac/versal_edac.c:848) is the .write handler of the debugfs file inject_ue (registered at drivers/edac/versal_edac.c:924 via edac_debugfs_create_file("inject_ue", 0200, ...), fops xddr_inject_ue_fops at :904 with .write = inject_data_ue_store), so count and buffer contents are attacker-chosen through write(2) by anyone with write access to the debugfs node (typically root / a user-writable debugfs mount). Violated invariant (validated-equals-used / terminator-slot accounting): line 859 len = min_t(size_t, count, sizeof(buf)) clamps count to at most sizeof(buf) == 6 WITHOUT the -1 (contrast the correct sibling pattern len = min(count, sizeof(buf) - 1) used in the same tree at arch/x86/mm/pkeys.c:147, kernel/dma/debug.c:756, drivers/usb/chipidea/debug.c:83, drivers/iio/industrialio-core.c:411, and ~50 ath/rtw89/amdgpu sites). Unsafe use: line 863 buf[len] = '\0' with len == 6 when the user writes >= 6 bytes writes one byte past the end of the 6-byte stack array (valid indices 0..5): a deterministic 1-byte NUL out-of-bounds stack write (KASAN stack-out-of-bounds / stack corruption) whenever count >= 6; count in 0..5 keeps it in bounds, which is why normal short 'echo 1,2' use never trips it. This settles the recorded f008-vs-f015 contradiction in favor of f015: f008's claim that 'an index bounded by sizeof(buf) = 6 stays in bounds' is wrong because buf[6] is one past the array. A C reproducer with the exact clamp+terminator lines compiled with AddressSanitizer under $TMPDIR reports 'stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1' at the buf[len] assignment. Counterevidence checked: the full function (lines 848-902) contains no count > sizeof(buf) - 1 rejection and no -1 in the clamp; the sibling inject_data_ce_store and inject_ce_write in zynqmp_edac.c use kstrtou8_from_user (no manual copy/terminate) and are safe. This is the seed's fix primitive (explicit NUL terminator slot) misapplied - the inverse of the seed's missing-terminator OOB read under the same terminator-slot accounting root cause. Impact is limited to a single controlled NUL byte one past a 6-byte stack array in a 0200 debugfs write path, hence reachability is root/debugfs-gated like the seed.

Untrusted source: inject_ue_write (drivers/edac/zynqmp_edac.c:294) is the .write handler of the debugfs file inject_ue_bitpos (registered at drivers/edac/zynqmp_edac.c:359 via edac_debugfs_create_file("inject_ue_bitpos", 0644, priv->debugfs_dir, edac_dev, &inject_ue_fops), fops at :343 with .write = inject_ue_write), so count and contents are attacker-chosen (0644 node under /sys/kernel/debug/edac/ocm). Violated invariant: line 307 len = min_t(size_t, count, sizeof(buf)) clamps to sizeof(buf) == 6 with no -1; line 311 buf[len] = '\0' then writes buf[6] when count >= 6 - one byte past the end of the 6-byte stack array (char buf[6], line 299). Unsafe use: the terminator write itself is the out-of-bounds store (1-byte NUL stack OOB write, KASAN stack-out-of-bounds / potential stack canary or adjacent-local corruption), before strsep/kstrtou8 consume the buffer. Same mechanism, byte-for-byte, as the versal_edac finding (lines 859/863), in the sibling Xilinx ZynqMP OCM EDAC driver. Counterevidence checked: full function read (lines 294-342): no count > sizeof(buf) - 1 rejection anywhere; the sibling inject_ce_write (lines 250-279) uses kstrtou8_from_user directly and is safe. The ASan harness for the identical clamp+terminate lines demonstrates the 1-byte OOB write. Reachability is root/debugfs-gated (0644 under debugfs), impact is one controlled NUL byte past a 6-byte stack array.

candidates.reason: buf[len] = '\0' with len = min_t(size_t, count, sizeof(buf)) on char buf[6]: len can equal 6, writing one byte past the array; reported as finding 1.
Identical clamp-without-minus-1 then buf[len] = '\0' on char buf[6]; reported as finding 2.
buf_size = min(count, (sizeof(buf) - 1)) (line 1257) before buf[buf_size] = '\0'; terminator index capped at sizeof(buf)-1, in bounds.
buf_size = min(count, (sizeof(buf)-1)) (line 312) before buf[buf_size] = 0; in-bounds terminator.
buf_size = min(count, (size_t)(sizeof(buf)-1)) (line 282) before buf[buf_size] = 0; in-bounds terminator.
count = min_t(size_t, sizeof(buf) - 1, count) (line 83) before buf[count] = '\0'; in-bounds.
len = min((size_t) 15, s) (line 137) with char buf[16] (line 130); buf[len] at index <= 15 is the last in-bounds byte.
size = min(sizeof(attr->set_buf) - 1, len) (line 120) before attr->set_buf[size] = '\0'; in-bounds.
count is capped to MAX_LINELENGTH - 1 (line 316-317 'if (count >= MAX_LINELENGTH) count = MAX_LINELENGTH -1;') before progress_led[count] = 0; in-bounds on the MAX_LINELENGTH array.
len = min(count, (size_t)(NAME_MAX_LEN - 1)) (line 756) on char buf[NAME_MAX_LEN]; buf[len] in bounds.
count >= PAGE_SIZE is rejected (line 101-102) and buf is a full __get_free_page page, so buf[count] with count <= PAGE_SIZE-1 is in bounds.
kernfs_fop_write_iter allocates kmalloc(len + 1) (or prealloc_buf sized likewise) and writes buf[len] = '\0' into the +1 slot; the underlying guarantee for all sysfs ->store buffers.
Sibling handler inject_ce_write uses kstrtou8_from_user(data, count, 0, ...) - no manual copy or terminator write at all.

limitations: The tree-wide sweep enumerated 2945 buf[idx] = 0/'\0' terminator-write sites via regex and triaged the ~418 whose index is count/size/len/cnt-family or min-clamped; every min-clamp site outside the two edac drivers uses the correct sizeof(buf)-1 (or equivalent -1) form (ath5k x6, ath6kl x7, ath9k, ath10k, ath11k, rtw89 x7, amdgpu_pm, toshiba_acpi, ntb_tool, iio, pseudo_lock, regmap-debugfs, aat2870, chipidea, hid-wiimote, spufs, dma-debug, nf_conntrack_amanda, pktgen, kdb, bpf helpers, plpks, ipl_vmparm, prom_init), so the two reported edac sites are the only clamp-without-minus-1 terminator writes found in s04.

Terminator sites whose index is a plain loop counter or a kernel-computed length (e.g. bcachefs/fs.c:1419 name[name_len] with name_len = min_t(unsigned, dirent_name.len, NAME_MAX) into name[NAME_MAX+1-class buffers]) were spot-checked as safe but not every one of the 2945 was deep-read; a site whose index derives from an unclamped user length through a helper (not a direct min_t/min assignment) could evade the regex window.

No kernel build or in-kernel KASAN run was performed (snapshot is read-only); the OOB classification for both findings rests on line-level bound analysis of char buf[6] plus an AddressSanitizer userspace reproducer of the exact clamp+terminator lines (reports stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1), not on a live kernel trigger.

Both findings are debugfs write paths (versal inject_ue mode 0200, zynqmp inject_ue_bitpos mode 0644 under /sys/kernel/debug/edac/), so practical reachability is root/debugfs-gated like the seed; impact is a single controlled NUL byte one past a 6-byte stack array, not a full arbitrary write.

The f008-vs-f015 contradiction is settled as f015 being correct: buf[len] with len == sizeof(buf) is one byte past the array, because valid indices of char buf[6] are 0..5; f008's 'safe' classification for the identical s04 versal_edac.c site is superseded by this artifact.
